question: first enterprise-domain full-population point on the V2 small tier (211 questions, all types)
design: all 211 enterprise questions, text-projection haystack (100 shared trajectories, 3,358 state documents), orchestrated retrieval (top-12), glm-5.3 answerer, deterministic evaluator specs (phrase-set/mc) with glm-5.3 llm judges for llm_* types; same runner protocol as the web-small text arm (0.1583)
findings: Enterprise lands at 0.190 vs the web text arm's 0.158 under the same protocol - same difficulty class; both sit far below the official reference frontier (RAG 51.0% .. Runbook-C 74.9%), consistent with V2 being built against agentic replay systems rather than plain retrieval.

The cost profile is the story for the LAFS framing: after the one-time corpus vector backfill (~88 min on CPU for 3,358 6k-char a11y documents), per-question p50 is 3.3s with the full orchestrated stack - two orders of magnitude left of the 26.9-177s reference band.

dynamic-environment (0.000, n=35) is the structural gap: those answers live in state transitions across observations, not in any single state's a11y text - the same class of gap the web domain's vision-needed stratum showed.
Abstention variants outperform their non-abstention siblings (0.333/0.333 vs 0.270/0.156): recognizing absence is easier than tracking state.
honest_reading: text-projection ceiling run, not a tuned system: plain orchestrated retrieval with no screenshots (enterprise has none in this tier's harness usage), no hub derivation, no PAR. 11/211 answers are empty generation degradations (recorded as wrong; 5.2%). Scoring mixes deterministic phrase-set matching with glm-5.3 llm judges for llm_* types; judge and answerer share the model family. CPU embedding device (the web arm ran MPS); ranking-shift-scale device differences apply per the 0.797/0.7669 precedent. First-question latency (5,303s) is the one-time corpus backfill and is excluded from the p50/p95 above.
